faehigkeiten.grund: Auslieferung wird je Abruf neu zusammengesetzt (adswizz vergibt je Abruf eine listeningSessionID, AIS leitet ueber hash_redirect um, Last-Modified liegt nur 0 s vor dem Abruf, Abruf laeuft ueber den Werbedienst simplecastaudio.com) - Byte-Offsets veralten (bei dynamischer Auslieferung sofort, gemessen 19.08.2026) und die Zeitachse verschiebt sich mit (eine Folge war 57 s kuerzer als 3,5 h zuvor), deshalb sind auch Sprungmarken in Sekunden unsicher

einzeiler: Examining Elon Musk's unprecedented political influence and tech empire
kurzfassung: Elon Musk has transformed his massive wealth and control over critical infrastructure into unprecedented political influence, donating hundreds of millions to the Republican party. Historian Quince Blodian joins the show to discuss Musk's strategy of entrenching structural dependency, his views on artificial intelligence, and his alignment with the tech right. They explore how Musk's worldview, shaped by concepts like simulation theory and cognitive hierarchies, challenges traditional democratic norms.
stichpunkte: Musk's record-breaking political donations make him the single largest donor in any election cycle.
His control over companies like SpaceX, Starlink, and X creates unprecedented structural and communicative dependencies.
Musk's political strategy involves high-risk alignment with far-right parties and hyperpolarization to shape future governance.
His approach to artificial intelligence has shifted from calling for safety regulations to building anti-woke models like Grok.
Musk's rapid wealth accumulation is driven by financial fabulousness and vertical integration rather than traditional profits.
His worldview combines elements of cognitive elitism, simulation theory, and a dismissal of traditional democratic norms.
Critics and economists debate potential countermeasures, ranging from heavy regulation to the nationalization of critical infrastructure.

clips.hook: Future reliance on Musk's infrastructure creates massive political risk
clips.text: Future administrations from various political backgrounds might view heavy reliance on critical technologies as a significant national security vulnerability.

clips.hook: A staggering surge to a trillion dollars in just six years
clips.text: A dramatic expansion in net worth over a very short timeframe highlights the extraordinary scale of modern tech wealth creation.

clips.hook: The empathy exploit as a fundamental vulnerability
clips.text: A critique of modern political dynamics suggests that compassion can be weaponized to undermine institutional stability and societal survival.

clips.hook: Absence of corporate succession planning at SpaceX
clips.text: Unusual corporate structures grant absolute voting control to a single individual without clear provisions for future leadership transitions.

clips.hook: A fifty-fifty split on living in a computer simulation
clips.text: Conflicting expert opinions from top scientists lead to a humorous middle-ground probability regarding the nature of reality.

beschreibung:
Ahead of the midterm elections, Elon Musk has become the single largest campaign donor in any election cycle, giving about $450 million to Republicans. It is just a fraction of a percent of his near-trillion-dollar net worth.
Musk’s control over SpaceX, Starlink, X, Tesla and Neuralink, on top of his riches, has given him power over wealth, attention and critical infrastructure that few human beings have ever amassed before. What does he want to do with all this power? What is he trying to buy with his campaign spending? What is the world he wants to build?
Quinn Slobodian is a professor of international history at Boston University. He’s the author of “Globalists,” “Hayek’s Bastards” and, most recently, “Muskism: A Guide for the Perplexed,” which he co-wrote with Ben Tarnoff.
Book Recommendations:
“Extraction” by Thea Riofrancos
“Silicon Empires” by Nick Srnicek
“Against Tech Oligarchy” by JS Tan and Clarissa Redwine
Thoughts? Guest suggestions? Email us at ezrakleinshow@nytimes.com.
You can find the transcript and more episodes of “The Ezra Klein Show” at nytimes.com/ezra-klein-podcast. Book recommendations from all our guests are listed at https://www.nytimes.com/article/ezra-klein-show-book-recs.html

Our recording engineer is Aman Sahota. Cinematography by Kyle I. Kelley. Video editing by Julian Hackney, Kristen Williamson and Arpita Aneja. Our executive producer is Claire Gordon. The show’s production team also includes Marie Cascione, Annie Galvin, Kristin Lin, Emma Kehlbeck, Jack McCordick, Marina King and Jan Kobal. Original music by Pat McCusker.
